title: Motor current correct
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (1) must be 0.2 A, derived from the voltage across R' and Ohm's law.

title: Input power correct
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (2) must be 1.44 W, calculated from the motor terminal voltage and current.

title: Heat power correct
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (3) must be 0.12 W, calculated using Joule's law (I²R) for the armature resistance.

title: Output power correct
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (4) must be 1.32 W, found by subtracting the heat power from the input power.

title: Apply circuit voltage law
description: Important: The solution must correctly determine the motor's terminal voltage (7.2 V) using the supply voltage and voltmeter reading.

title: Use energy conservation
description: Important: For part (4), the mechanical output power must be derived from the principle P_out = P_in - P_heat.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All final answers should include correct SI units (A, W, V, Ω) in calculations and results.

title: Confuse motor voltage
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly uses the supply voltage (8 V) instead of the terminal voltage (7.2 V) for power calculations.

title: Sign or subtraction error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student makes an arithmetic error in the voltage subtraction (8 V - 0.8 V) or the final power subtraction.
